93.proof: A sum of two rank-one three-tensors has every matrix flattening of rank at most2. Every tested triple has an explicitly computed nonzero3x3 minor in one actual flattening, hence tensor rank at least3. The given three-term expression supplies rank at most3, so every triple has tensor rank exactly3 over Q (and C). Thus none admits an exact local3-to2 replacement, with all other terms held fixed and no coefficient-alphabet restriction.
93.original_shortcut_justification: Three rank-one matrices b_i c_i^T are independent when both triples have pairwise nonproportional members: a nontrivial combination of two has matrix rank2 if both coefficients are nonzero, so cannot equal the third rank-one matrix. Zero coefficients reduce to forbidden proportionality. The factor-span shortcut was therefore valid here; direct minors independently avoid relying on it.
93.limits: Does not exclude modifying four or more terms, changing the full decomposition, approximate/border-rank constructions, or faster general matrix multiplication.
